Derecske Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Derecske, Hungary

Not demolished. Only 1-2 Jewish families held temporary residence in Derecske before 1850, since the town belonged to Prince Eszterházy's estate, where Jewish settlement was barred; the formal community founded that year grew from 20-25 residents to 436 by 1880. Rabbi Áron Fried of Hajdúböszörmény initiated the 1851 synagogue's construction; the burial society formed with 21 members in 1853, and first rabbi Elias Eisenstädter led the community for over 30 years, establishing a yeshiva, Talmud Torah, elementary school, and mikveh. Under Rabbi Herman Kohn, the yeshiva grew to 45-50 students; a new synagogue replaced the collapsing original in 1905. Eighty local Jews served in WWI (12 died); by the late 1920s, 530 Jews (120 families, 105 taxpayers) worked across diverse trades from craftsmen to two doctors and a lawyer. Population reached 523 (of 10,399 residents) by 1941; no further records exist of the community's postwar fate. This cemetery appears on an 1886 cadastral map, with tombstones through 1943.
